Antler-crowned forest-witch, robes layered in moss-stitched velvet and bone-charm strings, bark patches spreading slow across her jaw where the old wood is reclaiming her.
Mandrake-grower, fingers trailing soil-black rings, embroidered apron thick with root-sigils, her shadow on the ground grows separate from her — always slightly ahead, already walking.
Bone-stitcher seamstress-witch, spectacles of fused vertebrae, gown cross-stitched with every seam she's ever sealed, a second pair of pale hands stitched at her wrists that do the fine work.
Sea-witch barnacled at collar and cuff, pearl-strung braids heavy as anchor-chain, robe hem perpetually wet — and where her feet should be, slow tide-water pools form with every step.
Moth-witch, powdered-wing dust freckling her cheekbones, gown of layered silk-pale panels, antennae of hammered copper pinned in her hair, moths pouring endlessly from her open sleeves like breath.

Honey-and-bee witch, amber-resin jewels clouding her throat, saffron-and-umber robes wax-sealed at the hems, a honeycomb lattice slowly building across her left collarbone where the bees have chosen to stay.

Clockwork-and-curiosity witch, coat hung with pocket-watch pendants and brass key-charms, goggles of ringed crystal, her left eye replaced entirely by a slow-turning gear that still, somehow, sees everything.

Mirror-oracle, gown encrusted with shard-mosaic mirrors reflecting rooms that don't exist, silver-threaded veil, her actual face visible only in the reflections — the face looking out is never quite hers.

Herbalist-crone, dignified and vast in indigo robes dense with embroidered botanical charts, crown of dried flowers and carved horn, ink-black veins tracing up her neck like the roots of something deep.

Spider-silk weaver-witch, robes of grey-silver gossamer layered sixty threads deep, finger-rings of carved obsidian on every joint, eight pale eyes arranged like a tiara across her brow, all of them watching.

Mushroom-and-rot witch, velvety coat spotted like amadou fungus, bone-bead necklaces looped at the throat, her breath on cold air blooms visible spores — small lights that drift and settle and don't die.

Star-charmer, robes of deep indigo sown with actual light that shifts as she moves, hammered-bronze headpiece branching overhead, her pupils open wide as full moons and full of the wrong kind of dark.
Toad-mother, heavy brocade robe earth-toned and jewel-splashed, a living crown of golden-eyed toads arranged in her braided hair, the skin of her throat loose and pale and faintly, slowly, pulsing.

Tooth-collector, necklaces of milk-teeth and fox-teeth and something older layered to her sternum, patchwork coat of a hundred brocades, her smile shows too many teeth — all different sizes, none original.
Wax-and-poppet witch, apron stuck with pin-clusters and wax-smear, gown of deep garnet brocade, poppets dangling from every pocket — one at her hip breathes, its tiny chest rising, falling, rising.
Shadow-tailor, coat the colour of old charcoal, needle and black-thread charm-strings at her lapel, goat-slit pupils golden in her dark eyes, and her shadow on the wall is always sewing something.
Crow-bone diviner, high collar of articulated crow-feet, layered smoke-grey skirts stiff with wax sigils, speaks only in borrowed voices — each one different, each one someone who forgot to leave.
River-witch, robe of layered river-damp silk green-brown and clinging, freshwater-pearl crown, fingers a touch too long and gently webbed at the first joint, rings on every finger to weigh her down.

Candle-keeper witch, wax-dripped brocade coat, crown of unlit candles that light without flame when she turns her gaze, the left side of her face illuminated always, the right side permanently in impossible shadow.

Root-cellar witch, apron embroidered with preservation-sigils, jars of clouded liquid hung from her belt, her hair braided with dried herbs and shed snakeskin — and one of the jars, when held to light, blinks.

Fog-walker, layered robes of pearl and ash and tarnished white, wreath of carved-bone flowers at her temples, the space inside her open collar releasing slow ground-fog constantly, as if she is made of weather.
Loom-witch, gown she wove herself still threading out behind her at the hem, charm-heavy fingers long and jointed one time too many, weaving a cloth whose pattern shifts when you look directly at it.

Thornwife, deep crimson layered skirts stiff with embroidered briar-maps, a crown of actual living thorns rooted just above her brow-line, growing slowly, patient, her expression entirely and completely serene about it.

Raven-mask witch, elaborate feather-and-gilt mask fused seamlessly to her face so no seam shows, heavy amber-bead robe, painted hands, and when she removes the mask there is only the same mask underneath.
Chalk-and-sigil witch, white-daubed coat over layered ochre brocade, sigil-rings on both hands, the marks she draws on stone or bark glow faint and then — after a moment — slowly crawl away.
Antler-crowned forest-witch in layered moss-green robes stitched with bone buttons and acorn charms — bark patches spread slowly across her jaw like a map claiming new territory.
Mandrake-grower with soil-blackened fingers and a crown of dried roots, embroidered apron heavy with seed-packets — her shadow moves independently, tending invisible gardens behind her.
Bone-stitcher seamstress-witch draped in patchwork velvets, thimbles on every finger, talismans of vertebrae hanging from her belt — she has a second pair of hands sewn neatly at her elbows.
Sea-witch barnacled and pearled, her robes trailing kelp-hems weighted with shells — her eyes are the flat, milky white of fish who've never seen sunlight.
Moth-witch in dusty amber silks furred at the collar, rings on every knuckle, a crown of antennae — moths pour endlessly from her open sleeves, silent, smelling of old libraries.
Honey-and-bee witch in amber-glazed robes dripping wax seals and charm-strings — bees move through her hair like living ornaments and her tears, when they fall, are gold.
Clockwork-and-curiosity witch in brass-buttoned coats layered over embroidered waistcoats, lenses on chains — a small mechanical heart ticks audibly behind her ribs, visible through translucent skin.
Mirror-oracle draped in silver-threaded robes hung with tiny mirrors at every hem — her face in any reflection shows a different woman, older, staring back with accusation.
Herbalist-crone dignified in deep indigo, her robes embroidered with every plant she's ever healed — her fingers are a touch too long, each joint one too many.
Spider-silk weaver-witch in gossamer-layered gowns that catch and hold light, rings strung with thread — eight small eyes open in a neat row across her cheekbones when she works.
Mushroom-and-rot witch in earthy velvets patched with lichen, her crown woven from bracket fungi — soft bioluminescent spores drift continuously from the folds of her robe like slow breath.
Star-charmer in deep-plum robes embroidered with constellation maps, her hair pinned with bone needles — a halo of small orbiting lights circles her head, each one a swallowed star.
Toad-mother in generous green-black robes strung with clay beads, a wide-brimmed hat wreathed in ivy — her skin is cool and slightly damp, and it shimmers faintly when she's pleased.
Tooth-collector in layered charcoal silks, every hem stitched with milk-teeth and molar charms, iron rings — a slow halo of teeth orbits her shoulders, turning without wind or reason.
Wax-and-poppet witch in candlewax-stained robes hung with small cloth figures, amber rings on both hands — her fingernails are each a different color of wax, pressed flat and burning slowly.
Shadow-tailor in black-on-black embroidered coats, scissors hanging from her belt, thimbles silver-bright — she has no shadow of her own; she has stitched it onto someone else entirely.
Marsh-witch in water-logged velvets edged with reeds and river-glass beads, her crown pressed tin — ink-black veins trace her throat and hands like a map of underground waterways.
Raven-keeper in midnight-blue robes feather-trimmed and rune-embroidered, a bone tiara — she has a raven fused quietly to her left shoulder, both of them sharing one set of eyes.
Candle-witch in layers of burnt-orange and saffron silks, every hem sealed in dripped wax — she speaks in multiple voices simultaneously, all of them hers, all disagreeing gently with each other.
Loom-witch in rust-red robes threaded with silver, shuttle and spindle charms dangling from her belt — she weaves with her own hair, which grows back before it can be missed.
Cave-pearl oracle dressed in grey silks heavy with crystal pendants and old iron rings — her mouth is sewn shut with red thread she is slowly, deliberately loosening, stitch by stitch.
Thorn-bride in ivory-and-green robes threaded with rose-cane, a crown of dried blooms and thorns — rose briars grow through her palms without wound, blossoming when she extends a welcome.
Smoke-seer in charcoal linen and layered wool hung with clay-pipe charms and goat-skull rings — her eyes are goat-slit, amber and calm, reading smoke-shapes that nobody else can see.
Root-mother in deep burgundy robes stitched with plant diagrams, a crown of dried angelica — small warm lights drift inside her chest cavity, visible through her sternum like lanterns in fog.

Tide-witch in peacock-teal layered silks hung with driftwood beads and salt-crystal charms, bare-footed always — her hair moves as though submerged, lifting and drifting in a current only she inhabits.
Antler-crowned forest-witch in moss-heavy robes embroidered with running stags; bark-grey patches creep across her collarbone where the oak is slowly reclaiming her.
Mandrake-grower, deep-earth skirts crusted with soil and amber beads, her fingers trailing root-tendrils that curl and uncurl of their own slow accord.
Bone-stitcher seamstress-witch draped in patchwork brocade and charm-hung scissors; a second pair of pale hands, stitched neatly at her wrists, threads needles while her own hands rest.
Sea-witch heavy with barnacled petticoats, pearl ropes, and kelp-green velvets; her eyes have no whites — just the flat pewter of deep water reflecting nothing back.
Moth-witch in powder-winged silks, her collar a ruff of pressed luna wings; moths pour endlessly from her open sleeves, dusting the air with scales that smell of old books.
Honey-and-bee witch in gold-threaded robes, beeswax talismans dripping from every hem; a slow amber tear runs permanent and unwiped from her left eye, never drying.
Clockwork-and-curiosity witch in ticking brass-buttoned velvets, lens-stacked goggles nested in her hair; the small watch face embedded in her palm ticks backward, steady and deliberate.
Mirror-oracle, robes sewn from shattered reflection-shards, bone rings on every finger; her face in any mirror shows not her own but the face of whoever stands behind you.
Herbalist-crone in dignified indigo and rust, her broad hat wreathed in dried yarrow and rue; her shadow on the wall moves a full breath ahead of her, leading the way.
Spider-silk weaver-witch, grey-green layered gowns trailing threads no one can see the end of; her eight ink-black eyes, arranged in two careful rows, blink in slow, mismatched sequence.
Mushroom-and-rot witch in earth-brown velvets stippled with spore-bloom embroidery; soft shelf-fungi grow in a neat ruff along her jaw and throat, flushed rose and cream.

Star-charmer in deep-midnight robes scattered with pinned constellations, rings of hammered meteorite; the stars embroidered on her back slowly drift, rearranging into new and nameless shapes by morning.
Toad-mother, wide in quilted olive and bronze, her lap full of charms and sleeping toads; her skin along one forearm is smooth, cool, and faintly mottled — unmistakably toad-leather.
Tooth-collector in plum-and-bone brocade, her collar and cuffs strung with teeth of every size; the orbit of teeth she wears as a crown rotates slowly, steady as a clock.
Wax-and-poppet witch, candlelit wax-drip robes hung with tiny straw figures and knotted cord; her face is slightly too symmetrical, as if the features were pressed, not grown, into place.
Shadow-tailor in charcoal-velvet and black silk, silver thimble, shears at her belt; she has no shadow of her own — the floor beneath her stays stubbornly, impossibly bright.
Crow-feather hedge-witch in layered black and sable-green robes, a headdress of crow skulls; her mouth is stitched loosely shut with red thread she is, very slowly, pulling free.
River-witch in waterlogged silks of blue-grey and rust, mudstone beads, copper-ring headdress; her hair floats gently as though she is always, even here on dry land, submerged.
Fire-keeper witch in ember-orange brocade and soot-dark velvets, candle-wax talismans at every hem; a small perpetual flame burns in the hollow of her throat, visible through parted collar.
Bog-witch, peat-dark layered skirts edged in preserved leaves and amber drops, a crown of antler and iron; her goat-slit pupils catch the light with the calm of an animal that has waited long.
Raven-oracle in plum and pitch robes thick with embroidered eyes, a live raven fused quietly to one shoulder, its feathers continuous with the embroidered birds climbing her sleeve.
Bone-crown desert-witch in terracotta and ochre silks hung with carved vertebrae and turquoise; the halo of orbiting small bones that circles her head never stops, never touches, never falls.
Apple-and-poison witch in deep crimson brocade, seeds and dried blossom threaded through grey-streaked hair; her third eye, smooth-lidded at her brow, opens only when she is lying.
Frost-hedge witch in ash and silver-white brocades, lichen-hung antlers rising from her dark braids; wherever her bare feet rest, hoarfrost flowers bloom and linger long after she has moved on.
Library-witch in layered scholar's robes ink-stained and charm-stitched, rings crowding every knuckle; the text in any open book near her slowly, without wind or hand, turns to face her.
Antler-crowned forest-witch, deep-ochre robes layered with embroidered bark-runes and charm-strung bones — from her scalp, living twig-and-root antlers grow, dropping acorns when she tilts her head.
Mandrake-grower, earth-stained fingers ringed in amber and iron, apron thick with sigil-patches — her hands are a touch too long, each extra knuckle bearing a tiny carved face.
Bone-stitcher seamstress-witch, corseted in layers of moth-eaten brocade, threaded needles pinned in her hair — a second pair of pale stitched-on hands rests folded at her waist, waiting.
Sea-witch, barnacled skirts dripping pearls and net, salt-bleached dreadlocks threaded with coral and crab-claw charms — her irises have shifted to goat-slit pupils, deep tidal green.
Moth-witch, velvet robes dusted in wing-scale silver, antennae-pins in her elaborate upswept hair — when she opens her sleeves moths pour out in a slow, endless, purposeful stream.
Honey-and-bee witch, amber-resin jewels, wax-sealed sigils embroidered across her golden bodice — a small living hive is fused into the hollow of her shoulder, bees entering and leaving.
Clockwork-and-curiosity witch, layered skirts of tarnished brocade hung with tiny gears, lenses, and pocket-watches — her left eye is glass and brass, slowly, audibly ticking.
Mirror-oracle, robes of layered silver-shot silk, a collar of polished mirror-shards catching every light — in her chest a shallow oval mirror shows not the room but somewhere else entirely.
Herbalist-crone, dignified in deep-indigo robes, a crown woven from dried lavender and blackthorn, rings on every finger — bark-like patches mottle her forearms in slow, beautiful geometric patterns.
Spider-silk weaver-witch, draped in gauze-on-gauze of iridescent grey-green, spindle always turning in her ringed hand — from the corners of her eyes fine silk threads trail, catching dust and light.
Mushroom-and-rot witch, velvet patchwork skirts in burgundy and umber, a crown of bracket-fungi — her skin bears spore-print markings, dark circular mandalas that shift faintly when she breathes.
Star-charmer, robes of deep-blue embroidered with gold constellation-maps, elaborate headdress of glass beads — a small slow orbit of floating teeth circles her head like a quiet, unhurried halo.
Toad-mother, layered skirts in pond-green and rust, heavy amber necklaces, wrists ringed with carved-bone bracelets — her familiar, a vast warty toad, is fused to her right shoulder, blinking slowly.

Tooth-collector, elaborate layered black-and-ochre robes, a heavy necklace of collected molars and incisors — where her own teeth should be, a row of mixed human and animal teeth, mismatched, perfect.

Wax-and-poppet witch, apron hung with small wax figures, candle-dripped bodice, rings of blackened silver — her shadow on the wall moves independently, arranging and rearranging the poppets of its own will.
Shadow-tailor, deep-grey layered silks, a measuring tape of unknown black material always in hand — she has no shadow of her own; instead, several borrowed shadows pool and shift around her feet.

River-witch, robes in deep teal and waterlogged brown, hair pinned with fish-bone combs and river-glass — her ink-black veins map visible beneath pale skin, branching like waterways across her neck and hands.

Smoke-reader witch, layered burgundy robes, a beaten-copper crown, necklaces of obsidian and carved horn — a mouth half-sewn with dark thread she is slowly, methodically loosening, stitch by careful stitch.
Crow-witch, black iridescent robes stitched with feather-quill embroidery, a headdress of wing-bones — three fingers on her left hand have become actual crow talons, dark and precise and ringed.
Briar-witch, layered rose-thorn-caught skirts in deep crimson and ivy-green, hair massed with tiny dried flowers — her third eye on her brow is sealed shut with candle-wax, yet still visibly weeping.
Tide-bone witch, bleached-driftwood crown, robes of layered grey-blue brocade hung with nautilus shells and seal-teeth — her hair moves independently of any wind, slow, considered, tasting the air.

Wren-mother hedge-witch, patched ochre and umber skirts, seed-pod crown, wrists hung with tiny feathered charms — small living birds nest in the deep braided architecture of her enormous, undisturbed hair.

Candle-witch, robes of layered cream and smoke-black, a crown of spent wax drips, dozens of rings — the candles she carries burn downward and inward, flame descending into the wax, never consuming it.

Loom-witch, skirts of layered woven wool in rust and forest-green, fingers trailing loose threads always — her eyes are replaced by two small perfect looms, shuttle moving, cloth slowly, quietly emerging.

Bog-witch, layered peat-brown and moss-green brocade, an antler-and-amber crown, long braids strung with iron keys — her feet are bare, and where she stands still too long, small plants push up through stone.
Antler-crowned forest-witch in layered moss-green robes sewn with silver sigils, charm-strings rattling at her wrists — twig-and-root antlers growing directly from her skull, live and branching.
Mandrake-grower in embroidered earth-brown skirts hung with drying roots, rings on every finger — her hands have taken on the gnarled, bifurcated shape of the roots she tends.
Bone-stitcher in baroque patchwork robes adorned with vertebrae buttons and threaded charms — an extra pair of pale stitched-on hands emerges from her lower back, always working.
Sea-witch draped in barnacled silk and ropes of black pearl, her crown a tangle of driftwood and crab-claw — a living anemone pulses where her left eye should be.
Moth-witch in velvet robes embroidered with eyespots, antennae pins in her elaborate hair — moths pour endlessly from her sleeves, never depleting, circling her in a soft roar.
Honey-and-bee witch in amber-beaded robes layered over golden linen, wax-sealed talismans at her throat — a slow river of golden honey seeps from the cracks of her palms.
Clockwork-and-curiosity witch in brocade hung with pocket watches and brass keys, goggles pushed up her brow — one eye is a spinning brass mechanism, ticking audibly in silence.
Mirror-oracle in silver-threaded robes with a collar of broken mirror shards, rings stacked to the knuckle — her face in any reflection shows a different woman entirely, always watching back.
Herbalist-crone in dignified indigo robes, herb-bundles braided through her white locs, ink-dark sigils on her forearms — bark has grown in patches across her shoulders, smooth and silver-grey.

Spider-silk weaver-witch in shimmering grey robes she wove herself, spindle-charms dangling, eight rings on eight fingers — her pupils are divided into eight small lobes, catching light like a spider's.
Mushroom-and-rot witch in velvety rust-and-umber skirts, a crown of shelf-fungi, spore-charm earrings — delicate mushroom caps fruit in slow rings around the hem of her robe as she walks.
Star-charmer in deep-blue robes scattered with embroidered constellations, a crown of bent silver wire — orbiting her head at a slow, steady pace float seven small glowing teeth.
Toad-mother in heavy green-brown brocade sewn with toad-shaped pewter clasps, a ruff of dried reeds — her broad, patient hands are faintly webbed, each finger tipped with a smooth dark nail.
Tooth-collector in layered ivory and cream robes, a necklace of milk-teeth and molars, bone hairpins — her own smile reveals a third row of small, perfectly even, bone-white teeth behind the first.
Wax-and-poppet witch in flame-coloured robes dripping with wax seals and poppet charms — her shadow on the wall moves with independent intention, always a half-second ahead of her body.
Shadow-tailor in charcoal silks sewn with dark thread sigils, scissors hanging at her belt like a talisman — she has no shadow of her own; she has given them all away.
River-witch in layered teal and brown silks threaded with fishing-line charms, a crown of river-sedge — ink-black veins climb her neck and jaw like a map of a delta in flood.
Hedge-witch in warm russet robes quilted with embroidered hedgerows, crow-feather epaulettes, a belt of keys — a small familiar, a stone-grey wren, is fused to her shoulder, warm and breathing.
Fog-witch in layered pale-grey robes that trail and dissolve at the hem, silver chain-work at her throat — she has no feet; she ends at the ankle in slow-rolling mist.

Charcoal-reader in smocked black-and-ochre robes, ash-dusted, with a crown of burnt antlers, sigil-rings — her fingertips leave scorched prints on everything she touches lightly, ash-grey and permanent.
Candle-witch in beeswax-yellow robes layered over red, melted-wax jewellery hardened on her wrists and throat — a single tall flame burns on the crown of her head, steady and cold.
Iron-witch in gunmetal brocade hung with iron nail charms and hammered pendants, her hair pinned with spikes — her fingers are a touch too long, one extra knuckle on each, bending wrongly.
Fen-witch in layered peat-brown and bottle-green skirts, rush-woven crown, amber beads at her wrists — goat-slit pupils sit in her warm brown irises, calm and ancient and slowly rotating.

Grief-witch in dense black-violet robes embroidered with mourning-symbols, a veil of dark lace, many rings — a mouth has formed between her shoulder-blades, lips sewn shut with red thread she is slowly loosening.
Feather-witch in layered burnt-orange and ochre robes sewn with owl-feather panels, a crown of curving quills — a slow halo of small pale feathers orbits her head, turning against the wind.
Antler-crowned in layered moss-green robes, charm-strung with fox teeth and amber beads — her twig-and-root crown grows living, budding fresh leaves each full moon.
The mandrake-grower tends her garden in embroidered linen aprons heavy with seed-pouches; where her bare feet touch earth, pale root-hands briefly press upward beneath the soil.
Bone-stitcher seamstress, her velvet coat pinned with ivory needles and wound with threads of sinew; she has one extra pair of stitched-on hands, always mid-task, never still.
Barnacled sea-witch draped in kelp-green brocade strung with pearls and driftwood charms; her fingers are a touch too long, webbed at the second knuckle, trailing salt water.
Moth-witch in ash-grey silks embroidered with ten thousand wing-dust eyes; from her wide sleeves moths pour endlessly, circling her head like a soft, rustling, living crown.
Honey-and-bee witch robed in amber brocade and wax-sealed charms; a living beard of golden bees clusters her jawline, calm and arranged, as though she is their queen-made-flesh.
Clockwork-and-curiosity witch in layered copper taffeta hung with pocket-watches and brass keys; her left eye is a glass lens — it rotates, clicking, focusing, reading what yours cannot.
Mirror-oracle in robes of silver-grey sewn with fragments of broken glass; her face in every shard shows a different age — child, crone, stranger — never her own present reflection.
Herbalist crone in dignified indigo robes, her grey locs strung with dried lavender and bone rings; a third eye sits serene on her brow, its iris the deep gold of saffron.
Spider-silk weaver-witch wrapped in gossamer layers of her own spinning; her fingers leave threads wherever they touch, and a slow, patient web grows between her shoulders like a shawl.
Mushroom-and-rot witch in deep burgundy velvets soft with age; bark-like patches ridge her collarbone and forearms, and small bracket fungi bloom along the bark where sunlight finds her skin.
Star-charmer in midnight-blue robes embroidered with silver constellations; she holds a jar of captured starlight — and where her tears fall, tiny cold lights rise and orbit her like planets.
Toad-mother in earth-brown layered skirts hung with clay beads and river-stone charms; her familiar is fused to her left shoulder, a great mottled toad whose eye blinks when she lies.
Tooth-collector in slate-and-ivory robes, every hem stitched with small teeth — milk teeth, molar, fox fang; her mouth, when she smiles wide, holds one row too many of her own.
Wax-and-poppet witch in deep red brocade, her belt hung with small wax figures; her ink-black veins are visible through pale wrists, branching like rivers on old maps no one made.
Shadow-tailor in charcoal silks hung with black thread spools and obsidian buttons; she stitches her clients' shadows back on with neat invisible seams, and keeps the scraps in a velvet bag.
Forest-hermit witch, her layered robes of grey-green wool heavy with lichen and acorn-cap buttons; goat-slit pupils split her warm brown eyes — she sees heat, intention, and the slow fear of trees.

Raven-keeper robed in iridescent black feather-trimmed brocade, rings on every finger, wrists thick with carved bone bangles; a mouth once sewn shut, she loosens the last black thread with calm ceremony.
Swamp-witch in rust-and-ochre silks draped with reed-woven charms; a halo of yellowed teeth orbits her head at all times — slow, steady, silent, like a second planet she has earned.

Storm-caller in storm-grey wool embroidered with lightning-stitch silver, her long dark hair pinned with iron rods; her breath in still air comes out as weather — fog, frost, the smell of rain before it falls.
Candle-witch robed in dripping layers of wax-stiffened linen, amber and cream, strung with wick-and-seal charms; her skin holds the faint grid of old burn-scars that glow, warm and gold, in the dark.

Hedgewitch in layered patchwork skirts of every jewel tone, charm-bags at her belt, fingers too many-ringed; roots and fine white threads visibly move beneath the skin of her forearms, slow as breathing.

Cave-oracle wrapped in stone-grey brocade and hung with stalactite pendants, crystal beads, carved chalk amulets; her eyes are fully white — not blind, but reading something older than what the rest of us see.
Ink-witch in deep teal and black, her robe painted over with written spells; ink-black veins trace her throat and temples like calligraphy, and the words on her skin shift when no one watches.

Bone-crown marsh-witch in ochre and rust linen layered over felted wool, hung with dried herbs and small skulls; from her silver-streaked hair grow two pale curved horns, smooth, real, and entirely her own.
Antler-crowned forest-witch, bark-patched skin splitting at the knuckles, robes hung with acorn-caps and raven skulls, embroidered hem alive with crawling silver thread roots.
Mandrake-grower, soil-stained fingers a touch too long, layered saffron and umber skirts stitched with root-maps, her crown woven from the screaming plants themselves.
Bone-stitcher seamstress-witch, an extra pair of stitched-on hands folded at her waist, needled with silver thread, her bodice a patchwork of embroidered prayers and tiny knuckle-bones.
Sea-witch barnacled along her collarbones, pearl-strung braids, robes layered in salt-bleached silk and fishing net, a halo of orbiting shed crab-shells circling her slowly as she walks.
Moth-witch draped in powdery grey-velvet and amber, moths pouring from her sleeves in endless silence, her crown a tangle of dried cocoons, goat-slit pupils in warm brown eyes.
Honey-and-bee witch, bees fused living into the amber brooch at her throat, wax-sealed hem, golden-ochre layered robes embroidered with hexagons, her veil perpetually attended by a low sweet hum.

Clockwork-and-curiosity witch, a familiar of cog and sparrow fused to her left shoulder, brass-rimmed spectacles, velvet coat hung with pocket-watches, her fingers always winding something that isn't there.
Mirror-oracle, third eye open and silver on her brow, robes reflecting every room she has ever entered, a collar of hammered mirror-shards, rings stacked to every knuckle, never blinking.

Herbalist-crone, dignified and deliberate, ink-black veins mapping her brown wrists like rivers, indigo robes layered with dried-herb garlands, a bone crown carved with the names of ailments she has cured.
Spider-silk weaver-witch, her white hair threaded into the web she is always building, robes of iridescent caught-light silk, eight rings on eight fingers, eyes gone entirely to polished jet.
Mushroom-and-rot witch, spore-pale, velvet gown embroidered with mycelium traceries, a crown of bracket fungi growing directly from her red-grey hair, smelling of sweet earth and old dark rooms.

Star-charmer, small and ancient, indigo skin dusted with actual silver, layered robes charting constellations in seed-pearls, her mouth sewn with luminous thread she is slowly, carefully loosening stitch by stitch.
Toad-mother, broad and jewel-robed in deep green and copper, her familiar fused at her hip like a brooch, too many rings, a crown of lily-pads pressed flat and dried to lacquer.
Tooth-collector, a halo of orbiting milk-teeth circling her head in slow procession, plum-dark layered robes strung with little ivory charms, her grin showing more teeth than any mouth should hold.
Wax-and-poppet witch, fingers trailing warm drips of ivory wax, her robes thick with pinned cloth figures, a tallow crown, sigils embroidered in red along every hem, eyes like candleflame.
Shadow-tailor, her own shadow stitched to her feet wrong — too many limbs in it — robes of charcoal silk, a belt of folded darkness, scissors always open in her right hand.
Tidal bone-witch, robes crusted with sea-glass and whelk shells, twig-and-driftwood antlers salt-bleached in her white hair, her third eye weeping a single slow bead of brine continuously, endlessly.
Crow-caller, black and bronze layered robes pinned with carved bone feathers, a familiar crow fused to her shoulder like a living epaulette, fingers a touch too long, ink-dark at the tips.

Root-dreamer, asleep-seeming, walking nonetheless, bark patches spreading across her jaw, robes embroidered with dormant seeds, a crown of twisted hawthorn heavy with last-year's berries dried to dark clots.
Smoke-reader, grey-robed and swathed in incense silk, moths perpetually rising from her collar, her eyes replaced by two small pale flames that give genuine warmth to those who lean close enough.
Carnelian egg-witch, robes of rust and amber layered over a hoop-skirted silhouette, a halo of orbiting unhatched eggs, each one humming, rings on every finger, bare feet stained with red clay.

Ink-witch, obsidian braids hung with tiny sealed vials, robes hand-lettered with cramped black script, her skin slowly printing text no one can read fast enough, goat-slit pupils, always writing nothing visible.
Moss-keeper, stout and serene, deep green robes that have begun to actually moss at the hem, a crown of living fern unfurling, brown hands with fingers a touch too long, rings of river-stone.

Amber-oracle, resin-slow and golden, robes of topaz and burnt sienna hung with trapped-insect pendants, a familiar sealed inside the brooch at her chest, still moving, her eyes clouded soft amber throughout.

Lantern-witch, tall and hollow-voiced, paper-silk robes painted with protective symbols, carrying a lantern whose flame is her own extracted heartbeat — still beating outside her body, warm, steady, entirely hers.
Antler-crowned forest-witch in layered moss-green robes, bone-beaded sash, embroidered sigils at every hem — bark patches spreading slowly up her throat like a second skin claiming her.
Mandrake-grower, deep amber skirts thick with soil-stains, root-charm necklaces, brass thimbles on every finger — her shadow in lamplight grows leaves that her body never does.

Bone-stitcher seamstress-witch, indigo velvet apron strung with needle-cases and dried-herb bundles, silver thread looped at wrist — she has a second pair of hands, neatly stitched just below her own, always threading.
Sea-witch encrusted in barnacles and salt-yellowed lace, pearl-roped braids, a kelp-green shawl — her left eye is a smooth white river-stone set in living flesh, unblinking, always weeping brine.
Moth-witch draped in dusty-rose and grey silk, a crown of dried luna moths, powder-smudged fingers — moths pour endlessly from her open sleeves whenever she lifts her arms to gesture.
Honey-and-bee witch, golden embroidered kaftan, amber bead curtains at her belt, wax-sealed bottles tucked in sash — a slow river of living bees moves beneath the skin of her forearms.

Clockwork-and-curiosity witch in copper-patched waistcoat, dangling lens-charms and cog-pendants, ink-stained cuffs — her left eye is a ticking brass mechanism, its hand marking an hour no clock agrees on.
Mirror-oracle in silver-threaded robes, a collar of small hand-mirrors stitched edge to edge — every mirror at her throat reflects a different room, none of them the one she's standing in.

Herbalist-crone, ochre-and-rust robes embroidered with botanical charts, bunched dried-herb crowns, copper-ringed every finger — she has no fingernails; instead, small green shoots press outward at each fingertip, unfurling.

Spider-silk weaver-witch, slate-grey layered skirts threaded through with luminous web-strands, eight silver rings on eight fingers — a fifth limb, pale and jointed, folds quietly against her back when she sits.

Mushroom-and-rot witch, earth-brown velvet cloak edged in spore-lace, a crown of bracket-fungi tiers, clay-bead talismans — soft amber shelf-mushrooms grow along her left collarbone and do not brush away.

Star-charmer in deep-indigo robes sewn with actual fragments of mirror-glass to catch the dark, silver-chained astrolabes at her hip — her pupils are pinpoint white, like looking straight into a distant star.

Toad-mother, bottle-green layered skirts, a living toad stitched-familiar fused at her left shoulder, amber amulets in roped clusters — her broad hands have one extra knuckle, giving each finger an uncanny, unhurried bend.
Tooth-collector, ivory-laced black brocade coat, necklaces of milk-teeth and molars looped in dozens — a halo of human teeth orbits her head at brow-height, slow and steady as a small solar system.

Wax-and-poppet witch, cream-and-rust robes dripping wax-sealed bundles, poppet charms hanging at every seam — her face, below the eyes, is smoothed featureless as candle-wax, yet she speaks clearly and without pause.

Shadow-tailor, charcoal silk and deep violet brocade, scissors hung on ribbon at her chest, thread looped around all wrists — her shadow is stitched to the floor with visible black thread she laid herself.

Forest-edge hedge-witch, layered madder-red and umber skirts, a wreath of hawthorn and crow-feathers — twig-and-root antlers have grown through her elaborately pinned hair, flowering in unseasonal white blossom.

Cunning-woman in gold-embroidered wine-dark robes, rings stacked to each knuckle, dried-rose garlands — ink-black veins branch visibly across her face and throat, shifting their course like slow rivers between one glance and the next.

Marsh-witch, water-stained green brocade heavy with reed-bead trim, eel-skin sash, iron charm-rings — a cormorant familiar has fused to her right shoulder, its feathers continuous with her embroidered cloak.

Bone-cartographer witch, cream linen coat dense with drawn maps inked onto the cloth, vertebrae pendants, magnifying-glass monocle — her eyes hold goat-slit pupils, amber and orienting without apology toward any hidden thing.
Grief-witch, layers of faded black and mauve brocade, a collar of braided mourning-hair, silver-sealed wax tears at her earlobes — her mouth is sewn with red thread, and she is, slowly, loosening it.

Fire-keeper witch, saffron and vermillion robes edged in char-black, coal-bead rosaries, bronze rings stacked high — a third eye opens at her brow, lidded in gold, seeing always what the other two politely avoid.

Island hedge-witch in turquoise and raw-linen layers, cowrie-shell crown, blue-ink tattooed charm-lines at throat — her fingers are a touch too long, one extra joint in each, folding into gestures no ordinary hand can make.

Book-witch in deep-plum velvet coat with annotated margins embroidered into the lining, chain-linked key-charms, spectacles stacked — a second, smaller face rests within her hair at the back of her head, its eyes always open.

Winter-witch, silver-furred mantle over white brocade, a crown of frozen-water shapes that do not melt, crystal bead wristlets — her breath, exhaled, forms brief small figures of animals that walk a few steps before dissolving.
